Flow.description:
WHAT IT DOES: Saves every Account a Nonprofit Cloud form produces - the Person Accounts behind Contact 1 and Contact 2, the organisation behind the Account rule, and the Household - and then runs whatever follow-ups the form template asks for: household membership, family relationships, campaign members. It is the NPC replacement for the packaged Upsert Account engine and follows it step for step, so anyone who knows the packaged flow can read this one.
HOW IT WORKS, STEP BY STEP: 1. The calling step (Process Account, or Process Person Account Primary/Alternate) has already mapped the form's answers onto an Account record and chosen the matching rules. This engine never second-guesses the step. 2. Blank values are stripped, so an empty answer never erases data on a record being updated. 3. If the record arrived with an Id, it is updated. Otherwise the duplicate checker runs with the matching rules the step passed in: one match is updated, several matches stop the conversion for a human to resolve (unless the template allows the most confident match), no match inserts. 4. The saved Account is read back fresh, because a save returns only the fields that were set, and everything after this point needs the record as it truly stands - above all a Person Account's PersonContactId, the Contact Id the submission stores. 5. The outcome is logged to the Conversion Log with the Log Conversion Event action; the platform event it carries tells the action which status and lookup fields to stamp on the Form Submission, which is how the controller knows this rule is finished. 6. Then the Switch router: every follow-up returns here when it is done, each outcome fires at most once per pass (the Was Visited conditions), and when nothing is left the flow returns to the controller. In order: a Household-mode Contact 1 with no Account yet looks for the family's existing Household (found: it is written onto the submission; not found: Contact 1's status is set back to Ready, and the Account rule creates the Household before Contact 1 comes through a second time to join it); a saved Household gets its Party Relationship Group; a person joins the submission's Account when Household mode or the Add to Account rules ask for it; Contact 2 is related to Contact 1; campaign members are chained.
WHERE IT FITS: Installed by the Form Template framework's conversion mappings (Form Template Conversion Mapping Default custom metadata), dispatched one rule per pass by the conversion controller, re-run safely by Reprocess because every write is an upsert and every error leaves the slot's status non-terminal. The heavy lifting - groups, memberships, relationships, finding a family's Household - lives in the four NPC Utility flows, which admins can also call from automation that has nothing to do with forms. Change the field mapping in the calling steps; change matching, saving or logging here; change how the records themselves are written in the utilities.

formulas.description: The Account this conversion has settled on: the submission's own, or the parent's for a related row.

formulas.name: IncludedInGroup
formulas.expression: IF({!PlatformEvent.Type__c} = {!Contact1_FieldApiName}, INCLUDES({!FormTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Contact1 👉 Included In Group'), IF({!PlatformEvent.Type__c} = {!Contact2_FieldApiName}, INCLUDES({!FormTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Contact2 👉 Included In Group'),false))

formulas.description: Which slot this pass is converting: the Account rule, or a person (Contact 1 / Contact 2).
formulas.name: Is_Account_Slot

formulas.description: Contact 1 of a Household-mode main submission is the head of household; the membership utility ignores this when the Household already has one.
formulas.name: Is_Head

formulas.description: Reads the template's Is Primary Group sub-rule for whichever slot this pass converts: the Household becomes the place this person's information rolls up.
formulas.name: IsPrimaryGroup
formulas.expression: IF({!PlatformEvent.Type__c} = {!Contact1_FieldApiName}, INCLUDES({!FormTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Contact1 👉 Is Primary Group'), IF({!PlatformEvent.Type__c} = {!Contact2_FieldApiName}, INCLUDES({!FormTemplate.Conversion_Rules__c}, 'Contact2 👉 Is Primary Group'),false))

formulas.description: What the submission stores for this slot: a person is stored by their Contact Id (a Person Account has one), an organisation or Household by the Account Id.
formulas.name: Log_Record_Id

formulas.name: OwnerKeyPrefix

formulas.description: Contact 1 as the relationship anchor: the parent submission's on a related row.
formulas.name: PrimaryContactId

formulas.description: The relationship the form captured, falling back to the free-text Other answer.
formulas.name: RelationshipValue

formulas.description: A person is matched on their Account, which the standard Contact rules can never match, so the Standard Person Account Matching Rule is always named for a person - once, beside whatever the step passed in (activate it and its duplicate rule in Setup; they ship inactive). NPC_Person_Account_Match rides along solely for package validation: build orgs have no Setup UI and standard rules cannot be activated by any API (#631), so the build-test scaffolding activates that twin there; in a customer org the name resolves to nothing and is inert. An organisation matches on exactly what the step passed.
formulas.name: Resolved_Matching_Rules
